extractor_migration_2026_08.note: dictionary.sha256 was re-pinned when extract_dictionary.swift (PDFKit) was replaced by extract_dictionary.py (pypdfium2). Geometry parity is exact (22496/22496 lines). Two dictionary rows differ from the PDFKit-era hash, both from the same mechanism: PDFKit's per-row column-1 line-box y for a headword anchor (e.g. 'BY (prep)') can sit up to ~2pt above or below pypdfium2's loose-char-box y for that same row, while column 2-4 body-text y values match exactly between the two extractors. When an anchor's y and the next column's first example line's y are within that ~2pt band, the anchor-boundary cutoff in build_dictionary.py's find_anchors() can land on either side depending on which extractor produced the y. The pypdfium2 attribution is the semantically correct one in both known cases.
reattributed_examples: 2-1-B10: 'DIVIDE THE VALUE BY TWO.' moved from 'butt (v)' ste_examples to 'BY (prep)' ste_examples, where it belongs.
2-1-N1: 'Neither unit must operate.' / 'Neither of the units must operate.' moved from 'need (v)' non_ste_examples to the two 'neither' (adj/pron) entries, where they belong.
